summary: Documented M2-S01 (access, owner metadata-builder, status tested). Re-rendered PLAN.md, which was stale against plan v5 for the third consecutive step; appended five decision entries and one planner open item to decisions.md; wrote four workbook rows — two in a new Section 3 file for the CustomPermission and the PermissionSet, two in the Other configuration default for package.xml and deploy-order.md; wrote two traceability rows (REQ-015 and REQ-016, minted and anchored in this run); compiled the step's one manual acceptance test into TC-M2S01-01 with two Given/When/Then criteria records; and set the step documented. Every sentence is sourced from plan.json, the step's three envelopes, tests/M2-S01/results.json and its captures, or the two metadata files and deploy-order.md read read-only for the target_value cells.
confidence_rationale: Step 11 MEDIUM on two of its three named conditions, the same two M1-S01 and M1-S02 hit, plus one specific to this step. (1) package.xml and deploy-order.md could not be placed in a numbered section without judgment and fell to the Other configuration artefact-level default; and inside Section 3, the CustomPermission needed a judgment call against Concept 2's description of Section 5 as carrying the validation rule's 'bypass reference (Custom Permission + Custom Setting)' — resolved to Section 3 per Step 4's access-type map, with the Section 5 counterpart named as M3-S01's. (2) REQ-015 and REQ-016 were minted in this run and anchored to requirement.md line ranges plus the clarifications that settled them, because this build still carries no requirement register. (3) CWB-PERM-001 could not be given a deploy-order number at all: the ten-position sequence has no slot for a CustomPermission, so it is reported per Step 5 rather than numbered. Not LOW: no row has an empty source_req_id, no verification cell is empty, the test results and every tester capture were readable, and re-running produces no duplicates.

process_observations.observation: This is the first step in the build whose deploy-order.md any gate confirms: M2-S01 declares it in outputs[], so check-outputs verified it and the step's manual test asserts its content. On both M1 steps the same file was undeclared and verified by nothing, which is decisions.md O-M1S02-02 and M1 report F-04. The pattern the planner was asked to fix is already fixed on this step.

The least-privilege claim in the permission set's own description is checkable from the file rather than asserted: four top-level elements, exactly one of the fourteen grant-bearing elements present, thirteen absent. That is why the manual test's file-checkable half needed no judgment to tick.

M2-S01 introduces no RTM orphan: both manifest member forms are byte-identical to their file stems, so check_rtm.py's two index keys agree. The build's three orphans are still M1-S01's and are unchanged at 3.

The step's manual test is the first in this build that a plan-verifier blocker rewrote into an assertion over artefacts the build actually produces. The rewrite is what made it tickable at all — the original asked for evidence of a PermissionSetAssignment, which a design-only build can never hold — and the tester had already captured every file-checkable half before this run started.

The M1 report's F-01 remedy names M2-S01 as the step carrying layoutAssignments; in plan v5 the profiles are M2-S03's and M2-S01 declares no Profile. The stale pointer has been copied into two human_gates[] notes — the milestone:M1 approval and the step:M2-S01 approval, whose note opens 'Profiles step.' — and those are written records of a human's decision, so they cannot be corrected by a re-plan. Recorded as O-M2S01-01.

process_observations.observation: artefacts/M2-S01/deploy-order.md states the custom-permissions checker 'reports Consumers: 0 and an INFO, and exits 0'. No INFO fired: that INFO is raised only for a permission defined but ungranted, and this one is granted. Recorded as D-M2S01-05 and in CWB-OTHER-007; the artefact is left byte-identical because this agent does not edit artefacts.

The escaped-pipe break in the three M1-S01 Other-configuration rows is now measured, not predicted. Assembling every workbook row into one ten-section staging document produced eleven check_workbook.py errors across those three rows — status read as 'REQ-005 \\', recommended_agent as 'REQ-003', recommended_skills as 'pending:M5-S03' — every column after the first escaped pipe shifted by one. With the Other configuration block placed before any canonical heading, the same document returns OK.

The M1-S02 doc-keeper envelope records exit 0 for its two per-file check_workbook.py runs. Re-run unchanged in this pass, both exit 1 — the finding counts it recorded (9 and 10, all 'Missing canonical section') are right, the exit codes are not. Noted rather than corrected: an earlier run's envelope is not this run's to rewrite.

Neither declared checker on this step reads package.xml — check_access_model.py matches only permission-set-shaped suffixes and check_custom_permissions.py reads the permission and the grant — so manifest correctness rests entirely on the always-on manifest check. Raised first by step-tester; carried into CWB-OTHER-006 as its own named gap rather than left in one envelope.

The integration identity needs API access and this permission set deliberately does not grant it, because nothing on file says where it comes from and ApiEnabled would fail the step's own checker. Nothing in the build will ever show that access as missing, so a deployer following these artefacts alone gets an intake identity that cannot call the API.

process_observations.observation: Case_Intake_Integration diverges from templates/admin/permission-set-patterns.md's Integration_<System>_Bundle form, and the step's templates[] is empty so no cited authority could settle it. Two agents have raised it and neither could adjudicate. M2-S02 and M2-S03 add five more permission sets; deciding the convention now costs one plan edit, deciding it later costs eight files.

The consumer names written into the CustomPermission's description are a forward reference to a step that has not run, taken from M3-S01's declared outputs rather than from any clarification. If M3-S01 renames a rule or adds a third, the description goes stale and no checker detects it — check_custom_permissions.py reads the grant, not the description text.

The M1-S02 run predicted that M2-S01 to M2-S03 would create the profiles and so make check_ac_format.py's persona warning resolvable. Both halves of that prediction are wrong for this step: M2-S01 creates no profile, and the persona is a release reviewer reading files from disk, who holds no permission construct in any org. All six warnings across the three steps' criteria records are the same inherent one.

The workbook row schema requires a named human as owner and explicitly not a team alias, but no source in this build names a person; both Section 3 cells carry Q56's and Q10's owner_role, Security architect, with the substitution stated in the cell. Unchanged from M1-S01 and M1-S02.

M2-S01 is documented and M2-S02 is the next step, but it carries human_gate: true and its step:M2-S02 gate is pending, so build_plan.py next returns an empty list with that reason printed. The loop is waiting on a human, not on an agent.
